title: Interference and Measuring in Other Bases
summary: HH = I, HZH = X and why the phase decides the outcome.
mission: Qubit 0 was prepared in |+⟩ or |−⟩, and you do not know which. Add gates and a measurement to find out: |+⟩ must give 0 and |−⟩ must give 1, every time. In other words, measure in the X basis.
hints: The ordinary measurement separates |0⟩ from |1⟩ and gives 50% for each outcome for both |+⟩ and |−⟩. Before measuring, you need a gate that takes |+⟩ and |−⟩ to different poles of the sphere.
The Hadamard does that: it takes |+⟩ to |0⟩ and |−⟩ to |1⟩ (remember that HH = I, and that H|1⟩ = |−⟩).
The solution is qc.h(0) followed by qc.measure(0, 0).

prediction.question: Does applying H and then S to |0⟩ give the same state as applying S and then H?
options: Yes: the order of the gates does not matter
No: H then S gives |+i⟩; S then H gives |+⟩
No: H then S gives |+⟩; S then H gives |+i⟩
prediction.explanation: H then S: |0⟩ goes to |+⟩ and S turns the vector a quarter turn, to |+i⟩. S then H: S does not change |0⟩ (it only changes the phase of |1⟩), so the Hadamard takes it to |+⟩. In general, different gates do not commute: the order matters.
